tldr: LiteWebAgent is an open-source suite for VLM-based web agent applications that provides an extensible core framework with planning, memory, and tree search, along with production-ready deployments via a Vercel-based web app and a Chrome extension.
contributions: An extensible agent framework that decouples action generation from action grounding, supporting FunctionCallingAgents and PromptAgents
Integration of agent planning, agent workflow memory (AWM), and tree search (BFS, DFS, MCTS) into the framework
Asynchronous APIs integrating with FastAPI for minimal-effort serverless deployment on platforms like Vercel
Two deployed systems: a production-ready Vercel-based web application with a remote browser, and a Chrome extension controlling an existing browser via CDP
methods: The authors designed a VLM-based web agent framework that decouples action generation from action grounding: the policy generates natural language actions via greedy decoding using function calling or prompting, then a separate grounding step transforms actions into executable Playwright code using webpage observations (Accessibility Tree, DOM, screenshots, SOM). They integrated agent planning (basic, high-level, and context-aware variants) and Agent Workflow Memory into the planning/replanning loop. For tree search, they implemented BFS, DFS, and MCTS where MCTS uses a VLM-based value function to score trajectories in [0,1] and balances exploitation/exploration via UCB selection.
results: The paper presents a fully functional open-source suite with a deployed frontend at lite-web-agent.vercel.app and code at github.com/PathOnAI/LiteWebAgent. The Vercel-based web app provides users with an agent-controlled remote browser via iframe, with voice integration (TTS/ASR via Deepgram), Set of Marks highlighting, and real-time visualization of intermediate steps. The Chrome extension controls existing browsers via CDP, preserving user sign-in state. The framework supports both synchronous and asynchronous APIs with serverless deployment.
limitations: The paper is primarily a system/framework description with no quantitative benchmark results reported. It acknowledges future work is needed for evaluation modules with new metrics, extension to multi-agent frameworks, and a production-ready web agent with tree search. The current implementation uses a simple baseline (recursive function calling) as the default approach.
